messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Reminder: Seminal Ideas & Controversies in Statistics
messages.subject_clean: Reminder: Seminal Ideas & Controversies in Statistics
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Analytical choices in epidemiology carry assumptions that deserve attention alongside the code used. Seminal Ideas & Controversies in Statistics: A Short Course is a 2-day seminar livestreaming November 3?4 with Roderick Little (Department of Biostatistics, University of Michigan). Likelihood inference and generalized estimating equations offer different approaches to analysing correlated data. Epidemiologists using R can draw on the comparison when choosing and explaining methods for longitudinal studies. The discussion of probability sampling and randomized trials also connects statistical inference with study design.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/seminal-ideas-and-controversies-in-stati-2
The seminar page includes the full schedule and registration details.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Director and Co-founder
Instats | instats.org

messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone 

We've just launched a major upgrade to the Instats AI Research Assistant, 
giving researchers free, 24/7 access to leading AI technology to help 
with research methods, coding, writing, and much more in any language.

The Assistant is built directly into our research seminars, so you can 
engage leading experts and not only ask questions but also get support with 
your own research. Whether it's understanding difficult concepts, 
generating or debugging code, interpreting analyses, or applications to 
your own research the new AI research assistant is here to help!

It's designed with researchers' privacy, security, and intellectual 
property in mind ? your chats live locally on your browser and are never 
used for AI model training.
Use it for free: We've made many our seminars including A Bit of AI ? 
Best Tools for Research 
<https://instats.org/seminar/a-bit-of-ai-best-tools-for-research-free-1?viewassistant=yes> 
and the AI Research Assistant available free of charge. Register for the 
seminar and start asking questions directly alongside the video.

The Assistant is also included at no cost when taking any of our Instats 
certification programs 
<https://instats.org/results?view=Seminars&nav=Certifications>. Instats 
members enjoy unlimited access to the Assistant and more than 500 
expert-led research training programs.

As an organization founded and led by academics, our goal is to make 
world-class research training and AI assistance accessible to researchers 
everywhere.

We hope you find it useful, and please feel free to share it with 
colleagues and students! 

Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Director and Co-founder

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] AI Agents for Reliable Research
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Researchers can retain scientific judgment while assigning bounded analytical tasks to AI agents. Harnessing AI Agents for Reliable Research is a seminar livestreaming November 4 with Hadi Fariborzi (Bissett School of Business, Mount Royal University, Calgary). Build agent workflows with fixed evaluation criteria and stopping rules to support reproducible analysis. Epidemiological researchers using R can apply validation checks to pipelines that rerun from raw data. Decision logs and concise output summaries make the steps easier to inspect.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/harnessing-ai-agents-for-reliable-resear
The seminar page includes the full schedule and registration details.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Director and Co-founder

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Data-Driven Methods for Deploying AI
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Reliable measurement matters when research moves from controlled settings into everyday environments. Data-Driven Methods for Deploying AI is a seminar livestreaming November 6 with Manish Chauhan (School of Physics, Engineering and Technology, University of York). Statistical divergence measures can quantify differences between simulated and observed data when evaluating AI systems. Epidemiological researchers can apply these diagnostics to wearable sensor data and assess how measurement error affects deployment. Bayesian estimation and uncertainty quantification offer ways to support inference when observations are sparse or corrupted.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/data-driven-methods-for-deploying-ai-1
Full details are available on the Instats seminar page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Director and Co-founder

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] online course - Markov and Hidden Markov Models in R
messages.subject_clean: online course - Markov and Hidden Markov Models in R
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
Would you like to learn how to analyse longitudinal data using Markov and Hidden Markov models?
 
Join our online course Markov and Hidden Markov Models in R, taking place on 19?22 January 2027.
 
The course introduces the theoretical foundations of Markov and Hidden Markov models, with a strong focus on practical applications. Through interactive sessions and hands-on exercises in R using the LMest package, you will learn how to specify, estimate and interpret these models, including extensions with covariates and applications to continuous, categorical and incomplete longitudinal data.
 
By the end of the course, you will be able to:

Understand the fundamentals of discrete latent variable models.

Estimate Markov and Hidden Markov models for continuous and categorical longitudinal data, including datasets with missing values.

Perform model selection and assess parameter uncertainty using bootstrap procedures.
 
Course website: [ https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/markov-and-hidden-markov-models-with-applications-in-r/ ]( https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/markov-and-hidden-markov-models-with-applications-in-r/ ) 
 
 
Best wishes,
Carlo

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Geographic and Intersectional Momentary Assessment
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Repeated observations can bring geographic context into studies of health inequality. Geographic, Intersectional Ecological Momentary Assessment is a 2-day seminar livestreaming November 11?12 with Stephanie Cook (New York University). Multilevel models for GPS-linked ecological momentary assessment can help epidemiologists examine how health experiences vary across places and people. An annotated R workflow uses simulated data to separate momentary exposure from persistent differences between individuals through person-mean centering. Participants also examine structural measures of neighborhood disadvantage and the limits of causal interpretation.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/geographic-intersectional-ecological-mom
Further information is available on the seminar page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Director and Co-founder

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Scientific Paper Writing from Data to Discussion
messages.subject_clean: Scientific Paper Writing from Data to Discussion
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Epidemiological findings become easier to assess when their presentation supports the research question. From Data to Discussion: Writing a Scientific Paper is a seminar livestreaming November 12 with Kristin Sainani (Stanford University). Clear tables and figures can help epidemiologists convey patterns in their analyses. The workshop examines how to write Results and Methods sections that connect statistical evidence with a reproducible account of the work. It also considers how to interpret findings in the Discussion without repeating the Results.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/from-data-to-discussion-writing-a-scient
Full details are available on the Instats seminar page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Director and Co-founder

messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] Applied Deep Learning for Epidemiological Research
messages.subject_clean: Applied Deep Learning for Epidemiological Research
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-EPI members

A reminder - Epidemiological analysis often requires careful choices about how to represent complex data. Applied Deep Learning for Scientific Research is a seminar livestreaming November 16 with Nikolay Oskolkov (Lund University). Autoencoders offer a way to reduce the dimensionality of complex biological data. Epidemiological researchers using R can consider these methods alongside the seminar's treatment of model evaluation and uncertainty when analyzing their own datasets. Practical examples also cover data integration and applications in personalized medicine.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/applied-deep-learning-for-scientific-res
Further information is available on the seminar page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Director and Co-founder
